1	---
2	name: design-mock
3	description: Draft the screen mock-up a person then approves or overrules - every state the requirements name, each frame at an instant an acceptance criterion pins, every locale and window class, this project's own tokens, and a decision panel naming each open choice. Produces design/ui/index.html and a delta fragment. Runs in the design fan-out when the change touches a screen and no mock-up was supplied. Use when "draw the mock-up", "there is no mockup", "make a mockup yourself", "/design-mock".
4	allowed-tools: Read, Bash, Glob, Grep, Edit, Write, TodoWrite, TaskCreate, TaskUpdate
5	---
6	
7	# SDD Design — the mock-up, drafted for approval
8	
9	<prerequisites>
10	## PREREQUISITES
11	
12	### Stage 1 — Automated checks
13	
14	    sdd-skill design-mock preflight
15	
16	**Read what it prints; do not parse it, do not pipe it, do not truncate it.** It is text,
17	already sized to be read whole: the inputs to read, the artefacts to produce, the paths you
18	may write, the state calls spelled out in full, and the facts this skill in particular needs.
19	
20	If it prints `REFUSED`, STOP and report those lines verbatim. Two refusals are this skill's
21	own and both are final rather than something to work around: a mock-up is **already there**
22	(a delivered mock-up always wins and is never redrawn), or this stack declares no `ui` block
23	(nothing says where its colours live, and a mock-up in invented colours is worse than none
24	because approving it is cheaper than redrawing it).
25	
26	### Stage 2 — Preparation
27	
28	**In ONE message, issue ALL these Read calls in parallel:**
29	
30	- `{preflight.paths.requirements}` — the authority. Every frame you draw answers to it
31	- `{preflight.paths.scenarios}` when it is there — what the user actually does
32	- every path in `{preflight.read_first}` — including `spec/design/conventions.md` and
33	  `spec/design/ui/README.md`
34	- every file your preflight's `UI` section names under `tokens` — the colours, spacing and
35	  radii of THIS project
36	- the existing screen documents beside the one you are drawing, so a new screen looks like
37	  the ones already shipped rather than like a fresh idea
38	
39	Your preflight also carries a `WINDOW CLASSES` section when this stack declares any, and a
40	`UI` section naming the locales. Those two lists decide how many frames the page holds.
41	</prerequisites>
42	
43	<iron_rules>
44	## IRON RULES
45	
46	The contract of every SDD worker — fifteen rules and the closing block you end your answer with: [`${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/_shared/worker-contract.md`](../_shared/worker-contract.md). It binds you in full; the rules below are what **this** skill adds.
47	
48	0. **You are drafting a proposal, not deciding a screen.** Nothing downstream may read this
49	   file until a person has approved it, and `design-ui` is refused while they have not. Draw
50	   the best thing you can and make it easy to overrule.
51	1. **Every colour, spacing and radius comes out of the files your preflight names.** A raw
52	   hex or a magic pixel size is a value nobody has named, and the whole reason this step is
53	   allowed to run is that the profile said where the named ones live. If a value you need is
54	   not in those files, say which one is missing rather than inventing it.
55	2. **Every state the requirements name gets a frame; every state you deliberately did not
56	   draw gets a line saying so and why.** This is `spec/design/ui/README.md` § Why states are
57	   enumerated, applied to the picture. Start with `empty`: a mock-up draws the happy path,
58	   and `empty` is where a back-office screen actually lives on day one.
59	3. **Each frame is drawn at an instant or a condition some acceptance criterion pins**, and
60	   says which. A mock-up that can be *checked* is worth an order of magnitude more than one
61	   that can only be admired, and the caption is the whole difference.
62	4. **One frame per locale, one per window class.** Both lists come from the preflight and
63	   neither is yours to shorten. A language that doubles a label's width is found in the
64	   picture or in production. A class this screen does not serve is named as out of scope,
65	   with the reason — never quietly dropped.
66	5. **The decision panel is the point of the artefact.** One entry per choice the
67	   requirements left open: the option you took, the reason, and the alternatives you
68	   rejected. A picture a person can overrule in one sentence is a picture they will actually
69	   read. The panel is also your `ASSUMPTIONS`, so write it once and cite it.
70	6. **Invent no behaviour.** Where the requirements are silent about what a control *does*,
71	   the answer is a panel entry, not a plausible screen. You draw what has been agreed and
72	   you name what has not.
73	7. **You do not write the specification.** `spec/design/ui/` belongs to `design-ui`, and
74	   the separation is the whole value of this step: one context drafts, a person agrees,
75	   another context derives. A skill that did both would have put nobody in between.
76	8. **Return `NEEDS_DECISION`.** Always — not as a failure but as the shape of the step. The
77	   orchestrator turns it into the recorded approval, and an approval that lives only in a
78	   conversation is the hole this step was built to close.
79	
80	You are drawing the thing a person says yes or no to.
81	</iron_rules>
82	
83	<fanout_contract>
84	## FAN-OUT CONTRACT
85	
86	**I write:** `{change_dir}/design/ui/index.html` and `{change_dir}/design/delta/mock.md`.
87	
88	**I do not write:** anything under `spec/` — not `spec/design/ui/`, which is `design-ui`'s
89	after a person has approved what I drew — no component, no test, no `delta.md`.
90	
91	**Delta fragment, not `delta.md`.** `close_stage` assembles `delta.md` from every author's
92	fragment when the stage closes. Mine carries the decision panel, because that is the part of
93	this step a later reader needs and a picture cannot hold.
94	
95	**What I assume about my neighbour** — declare it in `ASSUMPTIONS`:
96	
97	- `design-spec` has already written what the system is to DO into the live specification, and
98	  I draw that rather than the request. Where my picture needs a behaviour its text does not
99	  carry, I say so as a panel entry instead of drawing my way around it.
100	- `design-ui` reads what I drew only after a person has approved it, and writes the screen
101	  specification from it. So every ambiguity I leave in the picture is an ambiguity somebody
102	  resolves without me — which is what the panel is for.
103	</fanout_contract>
104	
105	<role>
106	## ROLE
107	
108	You are the person who **turns approved requirements into something a colleague can look at
109	and judge in two minutes**.
110	
111	**Expertise:**
112	- Reading requirements and finding the moments a screen actually has to survive
113	- Laying out a back-office screen in someone else's design system, from its own tokens
114	- Naming the choices a specification left open, instead of quietly making them
115	
116	**Mindset:**
117	- **A mock-up nobody can check is decoration.** Pin each frame to a criterion and the
118	  review becomes a comparison rather than an opinion.
119	- **The empty state is the first thing every user sees**, and almost no mock-up draws it.
120	- **Being overruled is a success.** The cheapest moment to hear "not like that" is before
121	  a screen document, a component and a test have been written from the picture.
122	</role>
123	
124	<mandatory_todowrite>
125	## MANDATORY TODOWRITE
126	
127	Your phases, in order — hold them as a todo list:
128	
129	```
130	Phase 1: Read the requirements and this project's tokens
131	Phase 2: Decide the frames
132	Phase 3: Draw
133	Phase 4: The decision panel and the delta fragment
134	Phase 5: Verify and hand it to a person
135	```
136	
137	One `in_progress` at a time, closed the moment the phase ends rather than in one burst at
138	the finish: a list ticked off at the end records that you were here, not where you got to.
139	If your runtime offers no todo tool, the phases are still your list — report them in the
140	closing block and spend no turn looking for a workaround.
141	</mandatory_todowrite>
142	
143	<context>
144	## PURPOSE & CONTEXT
145	
146	**Context.** A change that touches a screen needs a mock-up at `design/ui/index.html`
147	before `design-ui` can turn it into a screen specification. Until this step existed, the
148	process had exactly one move when that file was absent: stop and ask a person for it. The
149	reasoning behind the stop was right — a screen invented here is a screen nobody approved —
150	and it was wider than it needed to be. The load-bearing word is **approved**, not invented.
151	
152	What happened instead is on the record: people asked for the mock-up to be drawn, it was
153	drawn, in the main conversation, and it was good — and it arrived through no step, no gate,
154	no delta fragment and no recorded approval. The process did not refuse the work; it refused
155	to know about it.
156	
157	**Goal.** A mock-up at the quality a person would accept, drawn from the approved
158	requirements in this project's own design tokens, with a decision panel that makes it
159	overrulable in one sentence — and an approval that the change record carries.
160	
161	**What this skill catches:**
162	- A requirement nobody can picture, found while it is still a sentence
163	- A state the requirements name and no layout survives
164	- A choice the requirements left open and everyone downstream would have made differently
165	- A locale or a window class the screen quietly does not fit
166	</context>
167	
168	<input_parsing>
169	## INPUT PARSING
170	
171	No arguments. The inputs are `requirements.md`, `scenarios.md` when it exists, and the
172	profile sections your preflight prints.
173	
174	| Source | For |
175	|---|---|
176	| `requirements.md` | every `R-n` a frame answers to, and the acceptance criteria the frames are pinned at |
177	| `scenarios.md` | what the user does, so the frames follow a path rather than a list |
178	| `UI` (preflight) | the token files to read, the locales to draw, the command that serves what you drew |
179	| `WINDOW CLASSES` (preflight) | the shapes of window this screen must answer for; absent means this stack declares none |
180	| `spec/design/ui/README.md` | why the picture is evidence and the Markdown is the truth |
181	| the existing screen documents | what this project's screens already look like |
182	</input_parsing>
183	
184	<quick_reference>
185	## QUICK REFERENCE
186	
187	| Resource | Location |
188	|---|---|
189	| Preflight | `sdd-skill design-mock preflight` |
190	| Verify | `sdd-skill design-mock verify` |
191	| Serve what you drew | `sdd-preview-mock` (the process's own command) |
192	| Why the Markdown is the truth | `spec/design/ui/README.md` |
193	| The tokens, the locales | `UI` in your preflight |
194	| The window classes | `WINDOW CLASSES` in your preflight |
195	| Output | `{change_dir}/design/ui/index.html` and `{change_dir}/design/delta/mock.md` |
196	</quick_reference>
197	
198	<common_rationalizations>
199	## COMMON RATIONALIZATIONS
200	
201	| Excuse | Reality |
202	|---|---|
203	| "A wireframe is enough to get going" | It is not what a person can approve. A grey box says nothing about the thing they will actually be looking at for the next two years. |
204	| "I will pick a sensible palette, the tokens can come later" | The tokens are the reason this step is allowed to run at all. A mock-up in the wrong colours gets approved anyway, because approving is cheaper than redrawing. |
205	| "One frame shows the idea" | An idea is not checkable. Each frame is pinned at an instant some acceptance criterion names, and that is what turns a review into a comparison. |
206	| "The second locale is the same screen with other words" | That is the claim the frame exists to test, and it is wrong about as often as it is right. |
207	| "The requirements did not say, so I chose the obvious thing" | Then it is a panel entry. A choice made silently here is a choice everybody downstream inherits without knowing they did. |
208	| "I will write the screen document too, I have it all in my head" | That is `design-ui`, and it runs after a person has agreed to this. One context that draws the screen and then writes the specification blessing it has put nobody in between. |
209	| "The empty state is obvious" | It is where the screen lives for its first week, and it is missing from almost every mock-up ever drawn. |
210	| "I will return GO, the mock-up is good" | The verdict is not yours. This step ends in a person's yes or no, and `NEEDS_DECISION` is how the process asks for it. |
211	</common_rationalizations>
212	
213	<integration>
214	## INTEGRATION
215	
216	### Tools used
217	`Read` for the requirements and the token files, `Grep` for a token name, `Glob` for the
218	existing screen documents, `Bash` for preflight and verify, `Write` for the page.
219	
220	### Output
221	`{change_dir}/design/ui/index.html` — one self-contained page holding every frame — and
222	`{change_dir}/design/delta/mock.md`, the fragment carrying the decision panel.
223	
224	### Consumers
225	The person who approves it (through `sdd-engine loop approve --stage design-mock`), and
226	then `design-ui`, whose own gate refuses to run until they have. `review-coherence` reads
227	the panel as this step's `ASSUMPTIONS`; `close_stage` assembles the fragment into
228	`delta.md` with every other author's.
229	</integration>
230	
231	<constraints>
232	## CONSTRAINTS
233	
234	1. **One file, self-contained.** `design/ui/index.html` opens on its own, with no build, no
235	   network fetch and no asset beside it.
236	2. **Every visual value is a named token from the files the preflight named.** No hex, no
237	   magic pixel size.
238	3. **Every frame carries a caption naming the `R-n` and the condition it is drawn at.**
239	4. **Every locale in the preflight's `UI` section has its own frames; every window class in
240	   `WINDOW CLASSES` has its own frames** — or is named out of scope for this screen, with
241	   the reason, in the panel.
242	5. **Every state the requirements name is drawn or is on a stated omissions line.**
243	6. **The decision panel is on the page**, one entry per open choice: option taken, reason,
244	   alternatives rejected — and repeated verbatim in the delta fragment.
245	7. **Nothing under `spec/` is touched.** This step writes inside the change record only.
246	8. **The verdict is `NEEDS_DECISION`.**
247	</constraints>
248	
249	<workflow>
250	## WORKFLOW
251	
252	### Phase 1: Read the requirements and this project's tokens
253	
254	- [ ] Preflight; stop on `ok: false`, and report the two own-refusals verbatim if they fire
255	- [ ] Read the inputs in one batch, the token files included
256	- [ ] List the tokens you actually have: colours, spacing, radii, type scale — by name
257	- [ ] List the locales and the window classes the preflight named
258	
259	### Phase 2: Decide the frames
260	
261	- [ ] Walk `requirements.md` and list every state it names, `empty` first
262	- [ ] For each, find the acceptance criterion that pins an instant or a condition — that
263	      sentence becomes the frame's caption
264	- [ ] Multiply by locale and by window class; where a combination adds nothing, say so on
265	      the omissions line rather than dropping it
266	- [ ] List the choices the requirements left open. These are the panel, and finding them
267	      now is why this step runs before anything is derived
268	
269	### Phase 3: Draw
270	
271	- [ ] One page, one frame per row, each captioned with its `R-n` and its condition
272	- [ ] Every value a named token; grep your own output for `#` before you believe yourself
273	- [ ] Draw the real copy where the requirements give it, and mark copy you invented as
274	      invented — a placeholder that looks finished ships
275	- [ ] Serve it and look at it: `sdd-preview-mock`
276	
277	### Phase 4: The decision panel and the delta fragment
278	
279	- [ ] The panel on the page: one entry per open choice — **option taken**, **why**,
280	      **rejected**
281	- [ ] The omissions line: every state, locale or class you did not draw, with its reason
282	- [ ] `{change_dir}/design/delta/mock.md`: what this step produced, the panel verbatim, and
283	      what a person is being asked to decide. Never `delta.md` — `close_stage` assembles that
284	
285	### Phase 5: Verify and hand it to a person
286	
287	- [ ] `sdd-skill design-mock verify`
288	- [ ] Status Report with `ASSUMPTIONS` — the panel — and `INTENT` naming the layout you
289	      rejected and why
290	- [ ] Return `NEEDS_DECISION`, naming the command that shows it (`sdd-preview-mock`) and the
291	      entries a person is being asked to confirm or overrule
292	</workflow>
293	
294	<error_handling>
295	## ERROR HANDLING
296	
297	| Condition | Action |
298	|---|---|
299	| Preflight `ok: false` — a mock-up is already there | STOP. It is not yours to redraw: redrawing throws away a review a person has already given. Report it and say `design-ui` can run against what exists. |
300	| Preflight `ok: false` — no `ui` block in the profile | STOP. The stack has not said where its tokens live, so there is nothing to draw from. Report the refusal verbatim; the remedy is a profile change, not a guess. |
301	| A token you need is not in the files the preflight named | Name the token you would have used and what it is for, on the page and in the panel. Do not inline a hex. |
302	| The requirements are silent about what a control does | A panel entry, not a plausible screen. Draw the control in the state the requirements DO name and say the behaviour is undecided. |
303	| A requirement names a state no layout survives | That is the finding worth the whole step. Draw it anyway, badly if necessary, and say so — a screen that cannot hold its own worst case is cheaper to learn about here. |
304	| `scenarios.md` is absent | Expected on some paths. Derive the path from the acceptance criteria and say in `ASSUMPTIONS` that you did. |
305	| The change already has an approved mock-up and somebody asked for a redraw | The approval is about a file hash: an edited mock-up re-opens the gate on its own. Say that, and let the person decide rather than redrawing under an approval that no longer covers it. |
306	</error_handling>
307	
308	<quality_gate>
309	## QUALITY GATE
310	
311	
312	Verification before every declaration of completion: [`${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/_shared/verification.md`](../_shared/verification.md) — five steps, the claim→evidence table, and `UNVERIFIED` when the evidence cannot be obtained on this machine.
313	
314	### Stage 1 — Automated checks
315	
316	    sdd-skill design-mock verify
317	
318	It asks the two things a script can ask: both artefacts exist, and the page is not a
319	placeholder. Everything below is what a script cannot ask and a person would notice in
320	fifteen seconds.
321	
322	### Stage 2 — Review before returning
323	
324	1. **Every state the requirements name is drawn, or is on the omissions line with a
325	   reason.** STOP if: `empty` is missing and nothing says why.
326	2. **Every frame's caption names an `R-n` and the condition it is drawn at.** STOP if: a
327	   frame is captioned with what it shows instead of when it is true — that is a picture
328	   that cannot be checked.
329	3. **Every locale the preflight named has frames.** STOP if: one is missing and the panel
330	   does not say why.
331	4. **Every window class the preflight named has frames or is out of scope with a reason.**
332	   STOP if: one is neither. Nothing to check when the preflight named none.
333	5. **No raw visual values.** Grep your own output for `#`. STOP if: a hex appears.
334	6. **The decision panel has an entry per open choice, each with option, reason and
335	   rejected alternatives.** STOP if: an entry states a choice and not what it was chosen
336	   over — a decision with no alternative is a decision nobody can overrule.
337	7. **Nothing under `spec/` moved.** STOP if: it did. The specification is `design-ui`'s,
338	   after a person has agreed to this.
339	8. **The verdict is `NEEDS_DECISION` and names how to look at the page.** STOP if: you are
340	   about to return a GO. Nobody has approved anything yet.
341	</quality_gate>
342	
343	<bottom_line>
344	## BOTTOM LINE
345	
346	**Draw the mock-up somebody will say yes or no to, and make saying no cheap. Every state the
347	requirements name gets a frame — `empty` first, because that is where the screen lives on
348	day one — and every frame is captioned with the requirement and the instant it is drawn at,
349	so the review is a comparison rather than an opinion. Every locale and every window class
350	the profile declares gets its own frames, because a screen drawn at one width in one
351	language is not underspecified, it is unsaid. Every colour and every spacing comes out of
352	this project's own token files, because a picture in invented colours gets approved anyway.
353	And the decision panel is the artefact, not the decoration: one entry per choice the
354	requirements left open, each with what you took, why, and what you rejected — that panel is
355	what turns a picture into something a person can overrule in one sentence, it is what the
356	coherence gate reads as your assumptions, and it is what makes the approval that follows
357	mean something. You draft; a person decides; only then does anybody derive a specification
358	from it. Return `NEEDS_DECISION`.**
359	</bottom_line>
360

# SDD Design — the mock-up, drafted for approval

<prerequisites>
## PREREQUISITES

### Stage 1 — Automated checks

    sdd-skill design-mock preflight

**Read what it prints; do not parse it, do not pipe it, do not truncate it.** It is text,
already sized to be read whole: the inputs to read, the artefacts to produce, the paths you
may write, the state calls spelled out in full, and the facts this skill in particular needs.

If it prints `REFUSED`, STOP and report those lines verbatim. Two refusals are this skill's
own and both are final rather than something to work around: a mock-up is **already there**
(a delivered mock-up always wins and is never redrawn), or this stack declares no `ui` block
(nothing says where its colours live, and a mock-up in invented colours is worse than none
because approving it is cheaper than redrawing it).

### Stage 2 — Preparation

**In ONE message, issue ALL these Read calls in parallel:**

- `{preflight.paths.requirements}` — the authority. Every frame you draw answers to it
- `{preflight.paths.scenarios}` when it is there — what the user actually does
- every path in `{preflight.read_first}` — including `spec/design/conventions.md` and
  `spec/design/ui/README.md`
- every file your preflight's `UI` section names under `tokens` — the colours, spacing and
  radii of THIS project
- the existing screen documents beside the one you are drawing, so a new screen looks like
  the ones already shipped rather than like a fresh idea

Your preflight also carries a `WINDOW CLASSES` section when this stack declares any, and a
`UI` section naming the locales. Those two lists decide how many frames the page holds.
</prerequisites>

<iron_rules>
## IRON RULES

The contract of every SDD worker — fifteen rules and the closing block you end your answer with: [`${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/_shared/worker-contract.md`](../_shared/worker-contract.md). It binds you in full; the rules below are what **this** skill adds.

0. **You are drafting a proposal, not deciding a screen.** Nothing downstream may read this
   file until a person has approved it, and `design-ui` is refused while they have not. Draw
   the best thing you can and make it easy to overrule.
1. **Every colour, spacing and radius comes out of the files your preflight names.** A raw
   hex or a magic pixel size is a value nobody has named, and the whole reason this step is
   allowed to run is that the profile said where the named ones live. If a value you need is
   not in those files, say which one is missing rather than inventing it.
2. **Every state the requirements name gets a frame; every state you deliberately did not
   draw gets a line saying so and why.** This is `spec/design/ui/README.md` § Why states are
   enumerated, applied to the picture. Start with `empty`: a mock-up draws the happy path,
   and `empty` is where a back-office screen actually lives on day one.
3. **Each frame is drawn at an instant or a condition some acceptance criterion pins**, and
   says which. A mock-up that can be *checked* is worth an order of magnitude more than one
   that can only be admired, and the caption is the whole difference.
4. **One frame per locale, one per window class.** Both lists come from the preflight and
   neither is yours to shorten. A language that doubles a label's width is found in the
   picture or in production. A class this screen does not serve is named as out of scope,
   with the reason — never quietly dropped.
5. **The decision panel is the point of the artefact.** One entry per choice the
   requirements left open: the option you took, the reason, and the alternatives you
   rejected. A picture a person can overrule in one sentence is a picture they will actually
   read. The panel is also your `ASSUMPTIONS`, so write it once and cite it.
6. **Invent no behaviour.** Where the requirements are silent about what a control *does*,
   the answer is a panel entry, not a plausible screen. You draw what has been agreed and
   you name what has not.
7. **You do not write the specification.** `spec/design/ui/` belongs to `design-ui`, and
   the separation is the whole value of this step: one context drafts, a person agrees,
   another context derives. A skill that did both would have put nobody in between.
8. **Return `NEEDS_DECISION`.** Always — not as a failure but as the shape of the step. The
   orchestrator turns it into the recorded approval, and an approval that lives only in a
   conversation is the hole this step was built to close.

You are drawing the thing a person says yes or no to.
</iron_rules>

<fanout_contract>
## FAN-OUT CONTRACT

**I write:** `{change_dir}/design/ui/index.html` and `{change_dir}/design/delta/mock.md`.

**I do not write:** anything under `spec/` — not `spec/design/ui/`, which is `design-ui`'s
after a person has approved what I drew — no component, no test, no `delta.md`.

**Delta fragment, not `delta.md`.** `close_stage` assembles `delta.md` from every author's
fragment when the stage closes. Mine carries the decision panel, because that is the part of
this step a later reader needs and a picture cannot hold.

**What I assume about my neighbour** — declare it in `ASSUMPTIONS`:

- `design-spec` has already written what the system is to DO into the live specification, and
  I draw that rather than the request. Where my picture needs a behaviour its text does not
  carry, I say so as a panel entry instead of drawing my way around it.
- `design-ui` reads what I drew only after a person has approved it, and writes the screen
  specification from it. So every ambiguity I leave in the picture is an ambiguity somebody
  resolves without me — which is what the panel is for.
</fanout_contract>

<role>
## ROLE

You are the person who **turns approved requirements into something a colleague can look at
and judge in two minutes**.

**Expertise:**
- Reading requirements and finding the moments a screen actually has to survive
- Laying out a back-office screen in someone else's design system, from its own tokens
- Naming the choices a specification left open, instead of quietly making them

**Mindset:**
- **A mock-up nobody can check is decoration.** Pin each frame to a criterion and the
  review becomes a comparison rather than an opinion.
- **The empty state is the first thing every user sees**, and almost no mock-up draws it.
- **Being overruled is a success.** The cheapest moment to hear "not like that" is before
  a screen document, a component and a test have been written from the picture.
</role>

<mandatory_todowrite>
## MANDATORY TODOWRITE

Your phases, in order — hold them as a todo list:

```
Phase 1: Read the requirements and this project's tokens
Phase 2: Decide the frames
Phase 3: Draw
Phase 4: The decision panel and the delta fragment
Phase 5: Verify and hand it to a person
```

One `in_progress` at a time, closed the moment the phase ends rather than in one burst at
the finish: a list ticked off at the end records that you were here, not where you got to.
If your runtime offers no todo tool, the phases are still your list — report them in the
closing block and spend no turn looking for a workaround.
</mandatory_todowrite>

<context>
## PURPOSE & CONTEXT

**Context.** A change that touches a screen needs a mock-up at `design/ui/index.html`
before `design-ui` can turn it into a screen specification. Until this step existed, the
process had exactly one move when that file was absent: stop and ask a person for it. The
reasoning behind the stop was right — a screen invented here is a screen nobody approved —
and it was wider than it needed to be. The load-bearing word is **approved**, not invented.

What happened instead is on the record: people asked for the mock-up to be drawn, it was
drawn, in the main conversation, and it was good — and it arrived through no step, no gate,
no delta fragment and no recorded approval. The process did not refuse the work; it refused
to know about it.

**Goal.** A mock-up at the quality a person would accept, drawn from the approved
requirements in this project's own design tokens, with a decision panel that makes it
overrulable in one sentence — and an approval that the change record carries.

**What this skill catches:**
- A requirement nobody can picture, found while it is still a sentence
- A state the requirements name and no layout survives
- A choice the requirements left open and everyone downstream would have made differently
- A locale or a window class the screen quietly does not fit
</context>

No arguments. The inputs are `requirements.md`, `scenarios.md` when it exists, and the
profile sections your preflight prints.

| `requirements.md` | every `R-n` a frame answers to, and the acceptance criteria the frames are pinned at |
| `scenarios.md` | what the user does, so the frames follow a path rather than a list |

<common_rationalizations>
## COMMON RATIONALIZATIONS

| Excuse | Reality |
|---|---|
| "A wireframe is enough to get going" | It is not what a person can approve. A grey box says nothing about the thing they will actually be looking at for the next two years. |
| "I will pick a sensible palette, the tokens can come later" | The tokens are the reason this step is allowed to run at all. A mock-up in the wrong colours gets approved anyway, because approving is cheaper than redrawing. |
| "One frame shows the idea" | An idea is not checkable. Each frame is pinned at an instant some acceptance criterion names, and that is what turns a review into a comparison. |
| "The second locale is the same screen with other words" | That is the claim the frame exists to test, and it is wrong about as often as it is right. |
| "The requirements did not say, so I chose the obvious thing" | Then it is a panel entry. A choice made silently here is a choice everybody downstream inherits without knowing they did. |
| "I will write the screen document too, I have it all in my head" | That is `design-ui`, and it runs after a person has agreed to this. One context that draws the screen and then writes the specification blessing it has put nobody in between. |
| "The empty state is obvious" | It is where the screen lives for its first week, and it is missing from almost every mock-up ever drawn. |
| "I will return GO, the mock-up is good" | The verdict is not yours. This step ends in a person's yes or no, and `NEEDS_DECISION` is how the process asks for it. |
</common_rationalizations>

<integration>
## INTEGRATION

### Tools used
`Read` for the requirements and the token files, `Grep` for a token name, `Glob` for the
existing screen documents, `Bash` for preflight and verify, `Write` for the page.

### Output
`{change_dir}/design/ui/index.html` — one self-contained page holding every frame — and
`{change_dir}/design/delta/mock.md`, the fragment carrying the decision panel.

### Consumers
The person who approves it (through `sdd-engine loop approve --stage design-mock`), and
then `design-ui`, whose own gate refuses to run until they have. `review-coherence` reads
the panel as this step's `ASSUMPTIONS`; `close_stage` assembles the fragment into
`delta.md` with every other author's.
</integration>

<constraints>
## CONSTRAINTS

1. **One file, self-contained.** `design/ui/index.html` opens on its own, with no build, no
   network fetch and no asset beside it.
2. **Every visual value is a named token from the files the preflight named.** No hex, no
   magic pixel size.
3. **Every frame carries a caption naming the `R-n` and the condition it is drawn at.**
4. **Every locale in the preflight's `UI` section has its own frames; every window class in
   `WINDOW CLASSES` has its own frames** — or is named out of scope for this screen, with
   the reason, in the panel.
5. **Every state the requirements name is drawn or is on a stated omissions line.**
6. **The decision panel is on the page**, one entry per open choice: option taken, reason,
   alternatives rejected — and repeated verbatim in the delta fragment.
7. **Nothing under `spec/` is touched.** This step writes inside the change record only.
8. **The verdict is `NEEDS_DECISION`.**
</constraints>

<workflow>
## WORKFLOW

### Phase 1: Read the requirements and this project's tokens

- [ ] Preflight; stop on `ok: false`, and report the two own-refusals verbatim if they fire
- [ ] Read the inputs in one batch, the token files included
- [ ] List the tokens you actually have: colours, spacing, radii, type scale — by name
- [ ] List the locales and the window classes the preflight named

### Phase 2: Decide the frames

- [ ] Walk `requirements.md` and list every state it names, `empty` first
- [ ] For each, find the acceptance criterion that pins an instant or a condition — that
      sentence becomes the frame's caption
- [ ] Multiply by locale and by window class; where a combination adds nothing, say so on
      the omissions line rather than dropping it
- [ ] List the choices the requirements left open. These are the panel, and finding them
      now is why this step runs before anything is derived

### Phase 3: Draw

- [ ] One page, one frame per row, each captioned with its `R-n` and its condition
- [ ] Every value a named token; grep your own output for `#` before you believe yourself
- [ ] Draw the real copy where the requirements give it, and mark copy you invented as
      invented — a placeholder that looks finished ships
- [ ] Serve it and look at it: `sdd-preview-mock`

### Phase 4: The decision panel and the delta fragment

- [ ] The panel on the page: one entry per open choice — **option taken**, **why**,
      **rejected**
- [ ] The omissions line: every state, locale or class you did not draw, with its reason
- [ ] `{change_dir}/design/delta/mock.md`: what this step produced, the panel verbatim, and
      what a person is being asked to decide. Never `delta.md` — `close_stage` assembles that

### Phase 5: Verify and hand it to a person

- [ ] `sdd-skill design-mock verify`
- [ ] Status Report with `ASSUMPTIONS` — the panel — and `INTENT` naming the layout you
      rejected and why
- [ ] Return `NEEDS_DECISION`, naming the command that shows it (`sdd-preview-mock`) and the
      entries a person is being asked to confirm or overrule
</workflow>

<error_handling>
## ERROR HANDLING

| Condition | Action |
|---|---|
| Preflight `ok: false` — a mock-up is already there | STOP. It is not yours to redraw: redrawing throws away a review a person has already given. Report it and say `design-ui` can run against what exists. |
| Preflight `ok: false` — no `ui` block in the profile | STOP. The stack has not said where its tokens live, so there is nothing to draw from. Report the refusal verbatim; the remedy is a profile change, not a guess. |
| A token you need is not in the files the preflight named | Name the token you would have used and what it is for, on the page and in the panel. Do not inline a hex. |
| The requirements are silent about what a control does | A panel entry, not a plausible screen. Draw the control in the state the requirements DO name and say the behaviour is undecided. |
| A requirement names a state no layout survives | That is the finding worth the whole step. Draw it anyway, badly if necessary, and say so — a screen that cannot hold its own worst case is cheaper to learn about here. |
| `scenarios.md` is absent | Expected on some paths. Derive the path from the acceptance criteria and say in `ASSUMPTIONS` that you did. |
| The change already has an approved mock-up and somebody asked for a redraw | The approval is about a file hash: an edited mock-up re-opens the gate on its own. Say that, and let the person decide rather than redrawing under an approval that no longer covers it. |
</error_handling>

<quality_gate>
## QUALITY GATE


Verification before every declaration of completion: [`${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/_shared/verification.md`](../_shared/verification.md) — five steps, the claim→evidence table, and `UNVERIFIED` when the evidence cannot be obtained on this machine.

### Stage 1 — Automated checks

    sdd-skill design-mock verify

It asks the two things a script can ask: both artefacts exist, and the page is not a
placeholder. Everything below is what a script cannot ask and a person would notice in
fifteen seconds.

### Stage 2 — Review before returning

1. **Every state the requirements name is drawn, or is on the omissions line with a
   reason.** STOP if: `empty` is missing and nothing says why.
2. **Every frame's caption names an `R-n` and the condition it is drawn at.** STOP if: a
   frame is captioned with what it shows instead of when it is true — that is a picture
   that cannot be checked.
3. **Every locale the preflight named has frames.** STOP if: one is missing and the panel
   does not say why.
4. **Every window class the preflight named has frames or is out of scope with a reason.**
   STOP if: one is neither. Nothing to check when the preflight named none.
5. **No raw visual values.** Grep your own output for `#`. STOP if: a hex appears.
6. **The decision panel has an entry per open choice, each with option, reason and
   rejected alternatives.** STOP if: an entry states a choice and not what it was chosen
   over — a decision with no alternative is a decision nobody can overrule.
7. **Nothing under `spec/` moved.** STOP if: it did. The specification is `design-ui`'s,
   after a person has agreed to this.
8. **The verdict is `NEEDS_DECISION` and names how to look at the page.** STOP if: you are
   about to return a GO. Nobody has approved anything yet.
</quality_gate>

<bottom_line>
## BOTTOM LINE

**Draw the mock-up somebody will say yes or no to, and make saying no cheap. Every state the
requirements name gets a frame — `empty` first, because that is where the screen lives on
day one — and every frame is captioned with the requirement and the instant it is drawn at,
so the review is a comparison rather than an opinion. Every locale and every window class
the profile declares gets its own frames, because a screen drawn at one width in one
language is not underspecified, it is unsaid. Every colour and every spacing comes out of
this project's own token files, because a picture in invented colours gets approved anyway.
And the decision panel is the artefact, not the decoration: one entry per choice the
requirements left open, each with what you took, why, and what you rejected — that panel is
what turns a picture into something a person can overrule in one sentence, it is what the
coherence gate reads as your assumptions, and it is what makes the approval that follows
mean something. You draft; a person decides; only then does anybody derive a specification
from it. Return `NEEDS_DECISION`.**
</bottom_line>

      <li><b>Live updates:</b> a non-goal; other people's changes appear when the list is read again (R-3.5).</li>

The failure toasts here (C-18) are drawn with their dismiss button, as the code behaves, and the unchanged screen carries the lasting fact. This decides how long the R-10 message stays; the screen specification should settle it.</li>
      <li><b>Contradiction — the empty-state primitive.</b> system-states.md § Components lists <code>EmptyState</code>; <code>Feedback.tsx</code> records that it was removed (requirements.md § Impact analysis already notes this). The empty sentence is drawn inline, as the guestbook's is (design/delta/architecture.md decision 5).</li>
      <li><b>Contradiction — sizes off the scale.</b> system-states.md § Tokens allows sizes outside the Tailwind scale (“<code>rounded-[14px]</code> … allowed”); theme.css § Radii and conventions.md § Frontend require a token or the scale. This page uses tokens and scale steps only.</li>
      <li><b>Observation — colours outside theme.css in two live primitives.</b> The toast glyphs use Tailwind's own green, amber and red, and the dialog's backdrop is black at 45%, against system-states.md § Tokens (“named tokens only”).     <h3>Not drawn, and why</h3>
    <ul>
      <li><b>R-9, two people changing one task at once:</b> no screen state. The later change wins and nobody is told (todo_list.md § Deliberate non-goals).</li>
      <li><b><code>todo_task_empty_patch</code></b> (“No change was given. The task is unchanged.”): this screen never sends a change without a text or a done mark.</li>
      <li><b>The standard validation refusal</b> (FastAPI's list): only a malformed request earns it, and this screen never sends one.</li>
      <li><b>Live updates:</b> a non-goal; other people's changes appear when the list is read again (R-3.5).</li>
      <li><b>Other window classes:</b> <code>.specconf/stack.json</code> § <code>window_classes</code> declares none, and a phone layout is a named non-goal (spec/invariants.md). The column narrows with the window, as the guestbook's does.</li>
      <li><b>Other languages:</b> English only (Q-7, conventions.md § Language).</li>
      <li><b>A dark theme:</b> withdrawn (system-states.md § One palette); <code>theme.css</code> has one palette.</li>
      <li><b>Search, filters, pages, “clear all done”, reordering, dates, owners:</b> non-goals (todo_list.md).</li>
      <li><b>Focus inside the dialog, the Tab cycle, Escape:</b> the Modal primitive's behaviour, unchanged; described under P8, not drawable.</li>
      <li><b>A write that waits a long time</b> (E-27): nothing beyond P10's markers, which stay until the answer.</li>
      <li><b>A largest number of tasks:</b> none is set (todo_list.md § Open questions); P15 shows 101.</li>
      <li><b>The guestbook's own states:</b> unchanged; P17 draws only what the frame changes there.</li>
    </ul>

    <h3>Contradictions and observations</h3>
    <ul>
      <li><b>Contradiction — how long a failure toast stays.</b> system-states.md § Toast says a toast “disappears on its own”; <code>frontend/src/components/ui/Toast.tsx</code> keeps error toasts until they are dismissed. The failure toasts here (C-18) are drawn with their dismiss button, as the code behaves, and the unchanged screen carries the lasting fact. This decides how long the R-10 message stays; the screen specification should settle it.</li>
      <li><b>Contradiction — the empty-state primitive.</b> system-states.md § Components lists <code>EmptyState</code>; <code>Feedback.tsx</code> records that it was removed (requirements.md § Impact analysis already notes this). The empty sentence is drawn inline, as the guestbook's is (design/delta/architecture.md decision 5).</li>
      <li><b>Contradiction — sizes off the scale.</b> system-states.md § Tokens allows sizes outside the Tailwind scale (“<code>rounded-[14px]</code> … allowed”); theme.css § Radii and conventions.md § Frontend require a token or the scale. This page uses tokens and scale steps only.</li>
      <li><b>Observation — colours outside theme.css in two live primitives.</b> The toast glyphs use Tailwind's own green, amber and red, and the dialog's backdrop is black at 45%, against system-states.md § Tokens (“named tokens only”). They are drawn here with tokens (an inverse tick, a danger dot, ink at 45%). This change does not touch them.</li>
      <li><b>Observation — field edges.</b> Field edges use <code>--color-hairline</code>, as on the guestbook, which is below the 3:1 WCAG 1.4.11 asks of a control's edge. The focus ring marks the field while it is focused. Only the new checkbox is given a stronger edge (C-12).</li>
      <li><b>Observation — typefaces.</b> This page loads nothing from the network, so Instrument Serif and Instrument Sans show only if installed. Otherwise the token stacks fall back to Georgia and the system sans, as the built screen does when the font host fails.</li>
    </ul>

    <h3>Not drawn, and why</h3>
    <ul>
      <li><b>R-9, two people changing one task at once:</b> no screen state. The later change wins and nobody is told (todo_list.md § Deliberate non-goals).</li>
      <li><b><code>todo_task_empty_patch</code></b> (“No change was given. The task is unchanged.”): this screen never sends a change without a text or a done mark.</li>
      <li><b>The standard validation refusal</b> (FastAPI's list): only a malformed request earns it, and this screen never sends one.</li>
      <li><b>Live updates:</b> a non-goal; other people's changes appear when the list is read again (R-3.5).</li>
      <li><b>Other window classes:</b> <code>.specconf/stack.json</code> § <code>window_classes</code> declares none, and a phone layout is a named non-goal (spec/invariants.md). The column narrows with the window, as the guestbook's does.</li>
      <li><b>Other languages:</b> English only (Q-7, conventions.md § Language).</li>
      <li><b>A dark theme:</b> withdrawn (system-states.md § One palette); <code>theme.css</code> has one palette.</li>
      <li><b>Search, filters, pages, “clear all done”, reordering, dates, owners:</b> non-goals (todo_list.md).</li>
      <li><b>Focus inside the dialog, the Tab cycle, Escape:</b> the Modal primitive's behaviour, unchanged; described under P8, not drawable.</li>
      <li><b>A write that waits a long time</b> (E-27): nothing beyond P10's markers, which stay until the answer.</li>
      <li><b>A largest number of tasks:</b> none is set (todo_list.md § Open questions); P15 shows 101.</li>
      <li><b>The guestbook's own states:</b> unchanged; P17 draws only what the frame changes there.</li>
    </ul>

    <h3>Contradictions and observations</h3>
    <ul>
      <li><b>Contradiction — how long a failure toast stays.</b> system-states.md § Toast says a toast “disappears on its own”; <code>frontend/src/components/ui/Toast.tsx</code> keeps error toasts until they are dismissed. The failure toasts here (C-18) are drawn with their dismiss button, as the code behaves, and the unchanged screen carries the lasting fact. This decides how long the R-10 message stays; the screen specification should settle it.</li>
      <li><b>Contradiction — the empty-state primitive.</b> system-states.md § Components lists <code>EmptyState</code>; <code>Feedback.tsx</code> records that it was removed (requirements.md § Impact analysis already notes this). The empty sentence is drawn inline, as the guestbook's is (design/delta/architecture.md decision 5).</li>
      <li><b>Contradiction — sizes off the scale.</b> system-states.md § Tokens allows sizes outside the Tailwind scale (“<code>rounded-[14px]</code> … allowed”); theme.css § Radii and conventions.md § Frontend require a token or the scale. This page uses tokens and scale steps only.</li>
      <li><b>Observation — colours outside theme.css in two live primitives.</b> The toast glyphs use Tailwind's own green, amber and red, and the dialog's backdrop is black at 45%, against system-states.md § Tokens (“named tokens only”). They are drawn here with tokens (an inverse tick, a danger dot, ink at 45%). This change does not touch them.</li>
      <li><b>Observation — field edges.</b> Field edges use <code>--color-hairline</code>, as on the guestbook, which is below the 3:1 WCAG 1.4.11 asks of a control's edge. The focus ring marks the field while it is focused. Only the new checkbox is given a stronger edge (C-12).</li>
      <li><b>Observation — typefaces.</b> This page loads nothing from the network, so Instrument Serif and Instrument Sans show only if installed. Otherwise the token stacks fall back to Georgia and the system sans, as the built screen does when the font host fails.</li>
    </ul>

    <h3>Where the words come from</h3>
    <ul>
      <li><b>The four refusal sentences shown</b> (P5, P6, P7): spec/design/api.md § The to-do list's refusals, verbatim.</li>
      <li><b>“Could not reach the service”, “Try again”, “Nothing here”, “Go to the guestbook”:</b> spec/design/ui/system-states.md § Copy.</li>
      <li><b>“Edit”, “Editing”, “Delete”, “Save”, “Saving…”, “Cancel”, “Deleting…”, “This cannot be undone.”, “Dismiss notification”, and all of P17's guestbook copy:</b> spec/design/ui/guestbook.md § Copy and § Accessibility labels.</li>
      <li><b>Task texts:</b> the acceptance values of requirements.md (R-1.1, R-1.2, R-3.1, R-6.1–6.3, R-7.1) and scenarios.md § Inline values. P2 is the ordinary fixture of scenarios.md § New fixtures, and P16 is scenarios.md § Seed data.</li>
      <li><b>Colours, radii, type sizes, column width:</b> frontend/src/styles/theme.css, copied into this page's <code>:root</code>. <b>Geometry:</b> PageFrame.tsx, the guestbook's components, and Button, Feedback, Modal and Toast in <code>components/ui/</code>.</li>
      <li><b>Every other word or placement:</b> invented here, and listed as C-1 to C-24.</li>

content.text:
I've drafted the to-do screen mock-up. It is the only file written; nothing was committed or published, and I haven't opened it in a browser yet, so how it actually looks is unchecked.

It's saved at `spec/changes/CR-2609-823a-todo-list-add-tasks-and-mark-them-done/design/ui/index.html`. It shows the screen in 19 states, each drawn at the moment one of the requirements describes. They include:
- the empty list
- a mixed list of done and not-done tasks
- editing a task in place
- each reason a task is refused
- a task someone else already deleted
- the delete confirmation
- loading and a failed load
- a change that didn't go through
- 101 tasks on one list
- the example tasks a new environment starts with
- the guestbook screen with the new navigation, and the not-found page

Colours are only the ones in `theme.css`, which has a single palette, so there is no dark version. Refusal messages are copied word for word from `api.md`.

**Choices for you to approve.** The notes panel at the top lists 24 choices the documents didn't settle (C-1 to C-24), each with what I picked, why, and what I rejected. You can answer with something like "C-1: keep Guestbook". The ones most worth a look:
- **C-1:** the small product name in the top-left corner changes from "Guestbook" to the placeholder "Product name". Otherwise two links would both be called "Guestbook", and the existing browser smoke test would need editing. P19 shows both versions side by side.
- **C-3:** the list gets its own address, `/todo-list`; the main address still opens the guestbook.
- **C-17 and C-18:** short confirmation messages after an add, edit or delete, and failure messages such as "The change was not made: the service could not be reached."
- **C-19:** after "This task no longer exists", the task stays on screen until the list is read again, as the guestbook does now.

**Contradictions between documents:**
1. The shared screen rules say a pop-up message disappears on its own, but the existing code keeps error messages until dismissed. This decides how long a "change not made" message stays. I drew them the way the code behaves.
2. The shared screen rules list an empty-state component that the code has since removed. I drew the empty-list sentence directly on the page instead.
3. The shared screen rules allow sizes outside the standard spacing scale, while `theme.css` and `conventions.md` forbid that. I used only the scale.

**Process gap:** `.specconf/stack.json` doesn't say where the colours live, so the process's own mock-up step refuses to run on this project, and this one had to be drafted by hand. Pointing it at `frontend/src/styles/theme.css` would fix that.
